as_of_note: Sourced CONTEXT, never a scoring input. Compiled 2026-10-30 by the United States source-audit lane. Monthly Energy Review values are EIA annual totals read from the keyless CSV export of each table on 2026-10-30; 2025 values are EIA's current estimates and are revisable. Refining capacity is a 1 January census (EIA-820). Omitted for lack of a figure read on an official page in this lane: world rank as a total energy producer and the US share of world natural gas production.

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 1.2, Total Primary Energy Production (TEPRBUS)
metrics.note: Fossil fuels 89.73, nuclear 8.20, renewables 9.24 quad Btu. 2024: 103.64.

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 3.1, Crude Oil Production, Total (PAPRPUS, 13,661.934 thousand b/d)
metrics.note: Crude oil including lease condensate; excludes natural gas plant liquids (7.52 million b/d in 2025, same table).

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 4.1, Natural Gas Production (Dry) (NGPRPUS)
metrics.note: Marketed (wet) production 43,229.11 Bcf in the same table.

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 6.1, Coal Production (CLPRPUS, 528,423.418 thousand short tons)
metrics.note: Annual Coal Report 2024 (final): 512.5 MMst from 524 producing mines; productive capacity 832.8 MMst, published by state only.

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 7.1, Electricity Net Generation, Total (ELETPUS, billion kWh)
metrics.note: Natural gas 1,807 TWh, nuclear 785 TWh, coal 737 TWh, wind 464 TWh, solar 296 TWh (Table 7.2a).

metrics.unit: GW (net summer capacity, end of year)
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Monthly Energy Review (release 2026-10-29), Table 7.7a, Total Electric, Net Summer Capacity (ELGBPUS, million kW)
metrics.note: Electric Power Monthly Table 6.1 gives 1,318,809 MW utility-scale net summer capacity at end-August 2026. EIA-860M September 2026 operating sheet sums to 1,417,017 MW nameplate / 1,324,125 MW net summer (all statuses incl. standby and out-of-service).

metrics.basis: operable atmospheric crude oil distillation capacity, barrels per calendar day (b/cd); 19,157,174 barrels per stream day on the same census
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Refinery Capacity Report 2026 (released 2026-06-26), Table 1 and per-refinery file; Form EIA-820
metrics.note: Operating 18,126,493 + idle 34,000 b/cd. 130 respondents, of which 124 have crude distillation capacity; the 124 per-refinery values sum exactly to the total. EIA monthly operable capacity was 18,012 thousand b/cd in August 2026 (Valero Benicia stopped refining after the census).

metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Liquefied U.S. Natural Gas Exports (annual series N9133US2)
metrics.note: EIA Today in Energy (2026-07-14) reports 15.1 Bcf/d in 2025, up 26%. 2024: 4,367,170 MMcf.

significance: In 2023 the United States was the world's largest oil producer, with 21.91 million barrels per day, 22% of world total oil production (EIA definition of oil, including other liquids).
In 2025 the United States was the world's largest LNG exporter: 15.1 Bcf/d, 26% of a record 56.3 Bcf/d of global LNG trade.
On 1 January 2026 US operable atmospheric crude distillation capacity was 18.2 million barrels per calendar day across 130 operable refineries, after two closures in 2025.
US primary energy production was 107.2 quadrillion Btu in 2025, of which fossil fuels were 89.7 quadrillion Btu.
